summary: Perceptual redaction playbook and sampled SIEM deliverable with field change log
description:
Issue summary: Customer requires a deliverable package to support an EU banking audit. They want a SIEM export sample and a 'perceptual redaction' playbook describing how Redwood redacts PII while preserving forensic utility. Impact: audit deadline in two business days; customer cannot complete their internal evidence review without an example export and redaction mapping. Environment: production tenant for NordBank EU (tenant-id: nb-eu-01) in eu-west. Request details below.

Requested timeline: initial sample by 2026-03-14 EOD EU.

Requested files and metadata: see requested_deliverables.

Notes: customer emphasized they need a clear change log for any fields that have evolved across schema versions in the past 90 days, plus a description of how timestamp canonicalization and timezone offsets are handled for replay and correlation across Splunk/SIEM. They also need HMAC-signed batch manifests for chain-of-custody proof and a minimal reproducible example showing reversible pseudonymization with key rotation metadata for legal review.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer call. NordBank EU needs a package for an external compliance review next week. I captured high-level requirements and shared a sample field map template.

2026-03-12 13:40 - EngSRE (S. Cho): Noted. We can generate a 7-day NDJSON sample with canonical UTC timestamps and a per-record HMAC. Need confirmation on which fields customer considers sensitive for perceptual redaction (PII vs contextual).

2026-03-13 08:21 - Aisha Patel: Customer clarified they need redaction for 'user_email', 'user_ip', 'session_token' and 'prompt_text' (prompt_text requires partial redaction preserving semantic buckets). Also they requested a CSV field-change-log for schema v1.8 -> v1.10.

2026-03-13 16:05 - Marco Alvarez: EngSRE to deliver NDJSON sample + signed manifest. Security to prepare a short playbook describing perceptual redaction approach and reversible pseudonymization example with rotated key metadata.
2026-03-14 10:32 - Security (L. Nguyen): Draft playbook uploaded to Confluence, shared for review. Requesting legal to confirm wording for reversible pseudonymization example.
2026-03-14 15:48 - Marco Alvarez: Compiling package. ETA for delivery to customer 2026-03-14 18:00 CET.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 12:30 - Runbook review: Found existing SIEM export pipeline supports NDJSON and compressed multipart delivery; supports per-batch HMAC signing using customer-supplied KEK wrapped keys.

2026-03-12 14:00 - Data sampling plan: Will produce a 7-day contiguous window sample (2026-02-28 to 2026-03-06) containing 1,000 events representative across success, error, and retry paths. Events will include tenant context but with real PII replaced by deterministic pseudonyms and an appended pseudonym_salt_version field.

2026-03-13 09:50 - Schema diff: Identified three field evolutions between v1.8 and v1.10: 1) 'user_agent' split into 'ua_browser' + 'ua_device', 2) 'request_id' moved from top-level to 'meta.request_id', 3) 'geo' structure flattened from object to string. Will include CSV change-log with examples.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Timestamp handling: Export pipeline converts all timestamps to RFC3339 UTC and includes original local_offset field when available. Will document correlation guidance for Splunk ingestion and include a sample SPL snippet for parsing offsets.

2026-03-13 15:00 - HMAC manifest: Will use platform signing key (KMS alias: projects/redwood/siem-sign-prod) to produce per-batch HMAC-SHA256, include manifest.json with batch_id, event_count, utc_start, utc_end, and signature.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Reversible pseudonymization example: Security produced a minimal python snippet demonstrating AES-GCM encryption of email values with a per-day KEK wrap and published KEK rotation table (dates and key IDs).
requested_deliverables: NDJSON SIEM export sample: 7 contiguous days, ~1,000 events, tenant-scoped, canonical UTC timestamps, gzip compressed
Per-batch signed manifest: JSON manifest with HMAC-SHA256 signatures and clear fields for chain-of-custody
Perceptual redaction playbook: 2-3 page document explaining algorithmic redaction vs deterministic pseudonymization and examples for prompt_text partial redaction
Field change log CSV: mappings and examples for schema v1.8 -> v1.10 covering three evolved fields
Reversible pseudonymization example: short code sample, key rotation table, and KMS alias references
Ingestion guidance snippet: Splunk/SIEM example queries for timestamp normalization and correlation with original offsets
acceptance_criteria: Customer (NordBank EU) confirms the sample data contains redacted fields as requested (user_email, user_ip, session_token, prompt_text partial redaction)
Signed manifest validates with platform key; customer can verify HMAC using provided public metadata
Field change log clearly demonstrates mapping for changed fields with sample input/output rows
Playbook explains tradeoffs and provides recommended settings for retention and reversible pseudonymization for legal review
Delivery occurs by SLA date 2026-03-14 and is uploaded to the shared secure S3 presigned link with audit trail
follow_up_actions: Post-delivery: Schedule 30-minute walkthrough with customer to explain playbook and sample (owner: Marco Alvarez)
Create internal KB: 'perceptual-redaction-playbook-v1' and link examples for future similar requests (owner: Security)
Verify manifest verification steps with customer and close any verification tickets within 3 business days
